source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An 8-year-old who had a tonsillectomy loves crispy tacos. When can the child safely eat rough, scratchy foods again?
options: Right away if there is no pain
questions.rationale: Rough, scratchy, and spicy foods are avoided for 3 weeks after tonsillectomy. Citrus is avoided for 10 days. Full liquids start on day 2, then soft foods as tolerated.
explanations: Correct: avoid rough foods for 3 weeks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q699 (PDF p. 921)
questions.quote: Rough or scratchy foods, as well as spicy foods, are to be avoided for 3 weeks after a tonsillectomy.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child awaiting umbilical hernia repair goes home. Which sign of strangulation should make the parents call the physician immediately?
questions.rationale: Signs of strangulation include vomiting, pain, and an irreducible mass at the umbilicus.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q701 (PDF p. 923)
questions.quote: signs/symptoms of strangulation, which include vomiting, pain, and an irreducible mass at the umbilicus.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The mother of a child with celiac disease asks how long the special diet is needed. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: Celiac disease is a lifelong intolerance to gluten (wheat, barley, rye, oats). Treatment is mainly dietary management with a gluten-free diet.
explanations: Gluten must stay excluded even after symptoms settle.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q703 (PDF p. 925)
questions.quote: The treatment of celiac disease consists primarily of dietary management with a gluten-free diet.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Parents are preparing children for an outdoor camp. Which statement shows they need MORE teaching on sun protection?
options: 'No sunscreen is needed on cloudy days.'
'I'll reapply it at least every 2 hours.'
'They will wear hats and long sleeves.'
questions.rationale: The sun's rays damage skin as much on cloudy, hazy days. Sunscreen is applied before exposure and reapplied at least every 2 hours, and protective clothing is worn.
explanations: Correct answer: UV rays penetrate clouds.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q744 (PDF p. 972)
questions.quote: The sun’s rays are as damaging to the skin on cloudy, hazy days as they are on sunny days.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement by parents of a child discharged after glomerulonephritis shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'We'll test the urine for albumin weekly.'
'She can start dance class next week.'
'We'll make sure she gets enough rest.'
questions.rationale: Children return to normal routines gradually, with adequate rest. Strenuous activity one week after discharge is too rapid. Daily BP checks and weekly urine albumin tests are appropriate.
explanations: Correct answer: too rapid an increase in activity.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q768 (PDF p. 998)
questions.quote: parents should allow the child to return to his or her normal routine and activities, with adequate periods allowed for rest.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Population Groups
questions.stem: A preschooler has an immunocompromising condition. Which type of vaccine should generally be AVOIDED?
questions.rationale: An immunocompromised child generally should not receive live or attenuated vaccines (oral polio, MMR, varicella). Inactivated vaccines such as DTaP and inactivated influenza are recommended.
explanations: Correct: live vaccines can cause disease in these children.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q775 (PDF p. 1005)
questions.quote: An immunocompromised individual under ordinary circumstances should not receive a live or attenuated vaccine.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 3-year-old with chickenpox scratches at night. Which statement by the mother shows the teaching worked?
options: 'I'll put cotton gloves on her at night.'
'I'll apply lots of cream all over her.'
'I'll give her warm milk at bedtime.'
'I'll keep her room warm and cozy.'
questions.rationale: Gloves stop scratching from damaging the skin. Large amounts of topical cream can cause toxicity, and a warm room worsens itching.
explanations: Correct: prevents skin damage from scratching.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q780 (PDF p. 1010)
questions.quote: Gloves will keep the child from causing an alteration in skin integrity from scratching.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 1-month-old is hospitalized with intussusception. Which measure BEST supports the parent-child relationship?
options: Advise the parents to rest at home
questions.rationale: Rooming-in reduces separation anxiety and preserves the parent-child bond. Sending stressed parents home does not support the relationship.
explanations: Correct: keeps parent and child together.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q893 (PDF p. 1135)
questions.quote: Rooming-in is effective for reducing separation anxiety and preserving the parent–child relationship.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Before an infant boy's inguinal hernia repair, which parent comment needs follow-up teaching?
options: 'He may not be able to father a child someday.'
'He can go home the same day.'
questions.rationale: The location of a hernia often worries parents more than the condition itself. The concern about future fertility is a misconception that needs follow-up.
explanations: Correct answer: a misconception to address.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q894 (PDF p. 1136)
questions.quote: The anatomical location of a hernia frequently causes more psychological concern to the parents than does the actual condition or treatment.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother says, 'I'm afraid my child will have another febrile seizure.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'Tell me what frightens you most about seizures.'
'Most children never have a second one.'
questions.rationale: An open-ended statement lets the mother express her feelings. Promising that a seizure will not recur, or dismissing her fear, blocks communication.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q931 (PDF p. 1175)
questions.quote: Option 1 is the only response that is an open-ended statement and that provides the mother with an opportunity to express her feelings.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: The mother of an infant with chalasia (reflux) says, 'I must be causing her to vomit.' How should the nurse interpret this?
options: Lack of bonding with the baby
questions.rationale: The vomiting is caused by a physiological problem, not by the mother. Blaming herself is an unrealistic expectation that can lower her confidence as a parent, so the nurse helps her see she is not responsible.
explanations: She accepts the problem but blames herself.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q933 (PDF p. 1177)
questions.quote: The misconception that the mother is responsible for the problem is an unrealistic expectation of self

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother of a preschooler with impetigo says, 'But my children take baths every day.' Which response is MOST therapeutic?
options: 'You're concerned about how she got impetigo?'
'We won't tell the day care why she's absent.'
questions.rationale: Paraphrasing the mother's statement addresses her concern. The other responses make the parent feel guilty and block communication.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q974 (PDF p. 1223)
questions.quote: By paraphrasing what the parent tells the nurse, the nurse is addressing the parent’s thoughts.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother and her infant have just tested HIV-positive, and the mother is crying. What should the nurse do FIRST?
options: Ask how she was exposed to HIV
Sit quietly and listen as she talks and cries
Call the HIV counselor right away
questions.rationale: After devastating news, the client needs someone present as she begins to cope. The nurse sits with her and listens. Teaching and referral come later.
explanations: Helpful later, but not her immediate need.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1020 (PDF p. 1293)
questions.quote: The nurse needs to sit and actively listen while the mother talks and cries.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding supports a diagnosis of irritable bowel syndrome in a child?
options: Profuse watery diarrhea with daily vomiting
Diffuse abdominal pain unrelated to meals
questions.rationale: IBS causes diffuse abdominal pain unrelated to meals or activity, with alternating constipation and diarrhea. Frothy diarrhea suggests lactose intolerance; ribbon stools suggest Hirschsprung's disease.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1088 (PDF p. 1370)
questions.quote: Irritable bowel syndrome causes diffuse abdominal pain unrelated to meals or activity.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child with rubeola (measles) has Koplik's spots. What does the nurse expect to see?
options: Red spots on the soft palate
questions.rationale: Koplik's spots appear about 2 days before the measles rash. They are small blue-white spots with a red base on the buccal mucosa, last about 3 days, and then slough off. Measles spreads by airborne particles.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1089 (PDF p. 1372)
questions.quote: These are small, blue-white spots with a red base that are found on the buccal mucosa.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding is MOST typical of von Willebrand disease?
questions.rationale: Von Willebrand disease mainly causes bruising and mucous membrane bleeding (nose, mouth, GI tract), and menorrhagia in females. Joint bleeding is typical of hemophilia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1091 (PDF p. 1374)
questions.quote: The primary clinical manifestations of von Willebrand’s disease are bruising and mucous membrane bleeding from the nose, mouth, and gastrointestinal tract.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Ely, 7, fell from a mango tree and is admitted with a head injury.
questions.stem: The nurse documents that Ely is 'obtunded.' What did the nurse observe?
options: He cannot think clearly or quickly
He does not recognize place or person
He sleeps unless aroused, with limited response
He responds only to vigorous pain
questions.rationale: An obtunded child sleeps unless aroused and, when aroused, interacts little with the environment. The other options describe confusion, disorientation, and stupor.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1093 (PDF p. 1376)
questions.quote: If the child is obtunded, the child sleeps unless aroused and, when aroused, has limited interaction with the environment.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Ely, 7, fell from a mango tree and is admitted with a head injury.
questions.stem: A CT scan shows a basilar skull fracture, and the physician notes Battle's sign. What will the nurse observe?
questions.rationale: Battle's sign is bruising behind the ear from blood leaking into the mastoid sinuses. 'Raccoon eyes' (periorbital bruising) is the other classic sign of basilar fracture.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1110 (PDF p. 1394)
questions.quote: Battle’s sign is the presence of bruising or ecchymosis behind the ear caused by a leaking of blood into the mastoid sinuses.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with kidney disease has a serum sodium of 148 mEq/L. Which finding does the nurse expect?
questions.rationale: Hypernatremia (above 145 mEq/L) causes intense thirst, oliguria, agitation, flushed skin, edema, dry sticky mucous membranes, and nausea.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1117 (PDF p. 1401)
questions.quote: Clinical manifestations include intense thirst, oliguria, agitation, restlessness, flushed skin, peripheral and pulmonary edema, dry and sticky mucous membranes

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which laboratory finding does the nurse expect in an infant with hemolytic disease of the newborn?
questions.rationale: Hemolytic disease causes anemia (red cell production cannot keep up with destruction) and hyperbilirubinemia, made worse by the newborn liver's limited ability to process bilirubin.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1118 (PDF p. 1402)
questions.quote: The two primary pathophysiological alterations associated with hemolytic disease are anemia and hyperbilirubinemia.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Bea, 5, has purpura and nosebleeds and is admitted for suspected idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP).
questions.stem: Which laboratory result is consistent with ITP?
options: A low white blood cell count
questions.rationale: ITP shows a low platelet count (usually below 20,000/mm3) as the only expected abnormality. A bone marrow exam shows normal or increased megakaryocytes.
explanations: Anemia occurs only with significant blood loss.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1137 (PDF p. 1423)
questions.quote: Thrombocytopenia is the only laboratory abnormality expected with ITP.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Bea, 5, has purpura and nosebleeds and is admitted for suspected idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP).
questions.stem: Bea is given IV immune globulin (IVIG). Which result shows the therapy is working?
options: A rapid rise in the platelet count
A drop in the white cell count
questions.rationale: IVIG usually raises the platelet count quickly by interfering with the destruction of antibody-coated platelets by macrophages.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1119 (PDF p. 1403)
questions.quote: IVIG is usually effective to rapidly increase the platelet count.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which urinalysis finding does the nurse expect in a child with acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis?
options: Clear urine with no red cells
Hematuria with red cell casts and protein
Large amounts of white cell casts only
questions.rationale: Urinalysis in poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis shows hematuria with red cell casts and proteinuria. BUN and creatinine rise if renal insufficiency is severe.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1120 (PDF p. 1404)
questions.quote: a urinalysis will reveal hematuria with red cell casts. Proteinuria is also present.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which test primarily confirms bacterial endocarditis in a child with fever, malaise, and anorexia?
questions.rationale: Diagnosis rests mainly on a positive blood culture and vegetations seen on echocardiography. ESR and CRP may support it, and the ECG is usually not helpful.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1121 (PDF p. 1405)
questions.quote: The diagnosis of bacterial endocarditis is primarily established on the basis of a positive blood culture

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: What is the PRIORITY problem for a child with juvenile idiopathic arthritis during a flare?
questions.rationale: All of these problems apply, but acute pain must be managed before the others can be addressed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1136 (PDF p. 1422)
questions.quote: acute pain must be managed before other problems can be addressed.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Luis, 5 weeks old, has projectile vomiting after feedings that is getting more frequent and forceful.
questions.stem: The nurse sees peristaltic waves moving left to right across his abdomen. Which condition is suspected?
questions.rationale: Pyloric stenosis causes forceful, nonbilious vomiting, constipation, visible left-to-right peristaltic waves, and sometimes an olive-shaped mass in the right upper quadrant.
explanations: Colicky infants eat well and gain weight.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1138 (PDF p. 1424)
questions.quote: visible peristaltic waves move from left to right across the abdomen.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Luis, 5 weeks old, has projectile vomiting after feedings that is getting more frequent and forceful.
questions.stem: Luis is scheduled for pyloromyotomy. Which preoperative intervention is MOST important?
options: Give enemas until returns are clear
questions.rationale: Before surgery the infant is usually NPO on IV fluids. The nurse monitors the IV, intake, output, weight, and urine specific gravity, and weighs diapers. Enemas would worsen fluid loss.
explanations: Infant is usually kept NPO preoperatively.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1159 (PDF p. 1446)
questions.quote: monitoring the IV infusion, intake, output, and weight and obtaining urine specific gravity measurements.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which cerebrospinal fluid result MOST supports bacterial meningitis?
options: Clear, with low protein and low glucose
Cloudy, with low protein and low glucose
Cloudy, with high protein and low glucose
questions.rationale: Bacterial meningitis shows increased pressure and cloudy CSF with high protein and low glucose, because bacteria consume glucose.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1139 (PDF p. 1425)
questions.quote: findings usually include increased pressure and cloudy CSF with high protein and low glucose.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A teacher reports that an alert, attentive 7-year-old often stares into space for a few seconds, then resumes activity. What should the nurse suspect?
questions.rationale: Absence seizures are brief (5 to 10 seconds) arrests of activity with a blank stare and loss of awareness. The child keeps their posture and resumes the activity as if nothing happened.
explanations: Presents with physical complaints before school.
Not brief staring spells with loss of awareness.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1141 (PDF p. 1427)
questions.quote: They consist of a sudden, brief (usually 5 to 10 seconds) arrest of the child’s motor activities accompanied by a blank stare and a loss of awareness.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A newborn has bilateral clubfoot. Which information should the nurse include in parent teaching?
options: Casting cures every case of clubfoot
Surgery is done in the first week of life
Casting starts at birth and lasts at least 12 weeks
Treatment waits until the child walks
questions.rationale: Casting begins at birth and continues for at least 12 weeks or until maximum correction. Corrective shoes or surgery (usually at 4 to 12 months) may follow.
explanations: Surgery is usually delayed until 4 to 12 months.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1154 (PDF p. 1441)
questions.quote: For the infant with clubfoot, casting should begin at birth and continue for at least 12 weeks or until maximum correction is achieved.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: An infant is admitted with pertussis. Which problem is the nurse's PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: Copious, thick secretions in an infant's small airways make air exchange the priority. Fluid volume deficit, not overload, is more likely because of secretions and vomiting.
explanations: Correct: airway clearance is the priority.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1158 (PDF p. 1445)
questions.quote: The priority problem for the child with pertussis relates to adequate air exchange.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A mother asks what 'carditis' means in her child with rheumatic fever. The nurse explains that carditis is:
options: Involuntary movements of the face and limbs
Inflammation of the heart, mainly the mitral valve
Painful swelling of several large joints
A pink, ring-shaped rash on the trunk
questions.rationale: Carditis is inflammation of all parts of the heart, mainly the mitral valve. Chorea, polyarthritis, and erythema marginatum are other manifestations.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1161 (PDF p. 1448)
questions.quote: Carditis is the inflammation of all parts of the heart, primarily the mitral valve
